intro: Everything you sell or stock, and what it sells for. A product is the family, such as a cordless drill; each variant is the item itself, such as the blue one, with its own code, stock and price at each place.
start: Add your first item with Add an item: a name, a price and how many you have.
If you have many items, bring them in from a spreadsheet with Import.
Add the services you charge for, such as delivery or labour, under Service items.
Check your prices on Price books, place by place, with what each item costs you and the margin.

articles.title: Add an item to sell
articles.summary: Three questions: what it is, what it sells for and how many you have. Everything else is decided for you, and you can change it later.

steps.rest: on Products, and choose Add an item — three questions.
as customers know it.
and what it costs you if you want to see the margin.

steps.lead: Enter how many you have now,
steps.rest: counted today, and the unit you count in.

steps.lead: Open More details if you need them:
steps.rest: kinds, barcode, reorder level, wholesale price or brand. None is needed to start selling.
It can be sold at once. Save and add another keeps the drawer open for the next one.

articles.after: The drawer says what it decided for you: where the stock is kept, the category, the currency, the unit and the code. Change any of it on the product.
tips: A code (SKU) is made from the name if you leave it blank, and never the same as another item's.
To stop selling something but keep its history, archive it. Deleting retires it for good.

articles.title: Add a product that comes in sizes or colours
articles.summary: Use the full form to set what the variants differ by, then add each variant with its own code, stock and price.

steps.rest: and choose Full form — every field.

steps.lead: Give it a name and a product code,
steps.rest: and choose its category.

steps.lead: Turn on Customers choose between variants,
steps.rest: then press + Add an attribute for each option, such as Size or Colour, with its values.
then Add a variant for each kind. Give each its stock and its selling and wholesale price at each place.
The product and its variants can be stocked and sold.

tips: A product sold one way still has one variant: the variant carries the code and the stock.
To add a variant later, open the product and press Add a variant.

articles.title: Bring in products from a spreadsheet
articles.summary: Download the template, fill it in or paste into the grid, and import new items, update ones you have, or both.

steps.rest: on Products.

steps.lead: Choose the place the stock is for.
steps.rest: Quantities and prices land there. The item itself belongs to the whole organisation.

steps.lead: Say what happens when a row is already in the catalogue:
steps.rest: add new items only, update the ones you have, or both.
fill it in and press Upload a file. Or type and paste straight into the grid.
Rows with a problem are shown, so you can fix them and try again.

tips: Rows sharing a name with a variant label become one product with several variants.
When updating, a blank cell changes nothing.
Save for later keeps the grid so you can finish it another time.

articles.title: Change what items sell for
articles.summary: Change one price where it stands, or re-price many at once by a percentage or an amount, and see every new price before you save.

steps.rest: Each row is one item at one place, with what it costs you, its selling and wholesale price and the margin.

steps.lead: Press a price to change it,
steps.rest: enter the new one and press Save the price.

steps.lead: To change many, tick the rows and press Re-price….
steps.rest: Choose the selling or wholesale price, by a percentage or an amount, and how to round.
then press Re-price. Nothing is saved until you do.

tips: Every change is kept in the price history, with who made it and why. Your settings may ask for a reason.
Where prices change by request, the buttons read Send the request and Ask to re-price, and the change waits for approval.

articles.title: Ask for a price change and follow it
articles.summary: Where prices change by request, a change waits for approval and applies on the day you choose.

steps.lead: Change the price on Price books
steps.rest: as usual, or open the variant on the item's page and press Change price.
and when it takes effect. Left empty, it applies the day the request is approved.
It goes to the approver, through the approvals inbox.

steps.lead: Follow it on Price change requests.
steps.rest: The tabs show those waiting for approval, waiting for their day, applied, rejected and called off.

tips: Open a request and press Call it off to withdraw it before it is decided.
A cost, and the first price of a new item, are not held to requests.

articles.title: Add a service you charge for
articles.summary: Delivery, labour or a call-out: work you charge for by time or by the job. It is not stock, so it has no shelf and no receipt.

steps.rest: on Service items.
It is shown on quotations, invoices and purchase requisitions.

steps.lead: Set the rate and what it is charged per:
steps.rest: an hour, a day, a visit, or the job as a whole. Each document can change the rate.

With Offered on, it can be chosen on new quotations and invoices.

tips: Switch Offered off to stop using it. It stays on the documents that already name it.
On a bill, a service posts to its own expense account.

articles.title: Add a unit, such as a crate or a carton
articles.summary: Say how many of another unit it holds, so you can buy in cartons and sell in each.

steps.rest: on Units of measure.

steps.lead: Write the new unit in a sentence:
steps.rest: its name, such as Carton of 20, how many it holds and of which unit.
It can be used on documents at once.

tips: Units are retired, never deleted: an order that says 4 crates has to go on saying so.
